parsed.attack: The dated, photographed, timestamped record of everything installed in a rental unit is already a shipped product category: Inventory Hive and InventoryBase build exactly that artifact for UK lettings, already capture appliance plates and serials, and already sell through letting agents, so adding 'the model reads the plate and names the parts that fit' is a single release on a workflow they own. On the self-serve side OpenRent and Landlord Studio already hold the single-unit landlord relationship and would add a property asset record as retention, and Google Lens gives the identification half away free today. The wedge therefore splits into a free commodity half and a half owned by compliance-driven incumbents with the channel, leaving a freemium conversion with nothing distinctive to charge for.
parsed.strongest_defence: Inventory reports are legal artifacts produced by an agent at check-in and check-out to settle deposits, priced per report and sold to agents rather than owned by the landlord, and they are not a living record the owner returns to when something drips three years later. Landlord SaaS monetizes rent collection and tax, where an equipment record carries no revenue line, and the professional-recommendation loop runs through plumbers and electricians, a channel none of these incumbents touch.
parsed.verdict_reason: Adjacent incumbents already own both halves of the wedge and have every commercial incentive to merge them, though none of them currently serves the one-unit owner as the customer of record.
